lesson_title: The Line at the Bottom of the Slip: VAT
hook_text: That VAT line on your slip? The shop keeps none of it.
clip_script: Read any till slip to the very bottom. There's a line marked VAT. You paid it — nobody asked your permission. And here's the twist: the shop kept none of it. The shop is a collector, not an owner. It lifts that money at the till, keeps it safe, and passes it to SARS. Now the sum almost everybody fumbles. A slip reads R3 680 including VAT — how much tax is buried inside? Nearly everyone takes fifteen percent of R3 680 and announces R552. Wrong. The fifteen percent was worked out on the SMALLER number, the price before tax. R3 680 is already the full parcel: a hundred parts of price plus fifteen parts of tax — a hundred and fifteen parts in all. So the tax is fifteen parts out of a hundred and fifteen: R480. Going up, fifteen on a hundred. Coming down, fifteen on a hundred and fifteen. And that money in the till? Trust money — it was never the shop's to spend.
visual_style: A till slip scrolling to its last line, the VAT entry pulsing; a wrong sum stamped red and swept away; a bar dividing into 100 teal segments and 15 amber segments to show the 15/115 logic; coins sliding from a till drawer into a SARS vault.
pacing: Slip reveal, myth-bust beat, clean visual derivation, chant landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never drop a VAT mark again.
